core_obligations: Choose elements g_1 to g_m whose images in A/I form an H1-regular sequence generating J/I, so that J is I plus the ideal they generate (proof lines 7503-7506).
For an element x of I cap J^2, write x as a sum of a quadratic combination of the g_i, a multiple of the g_i with coefficients in I, and an element of I^2 (proof lines 7506-7512).
Observe that the quadratic part lies in I cap the ideal generated by the g_i and apply the intersection lemma to place it in I times that ideal (proof lines 7512-7518).
Conclude that all three parts lie in IJ, hence x lies in IJ, which is the statement (proof lines 7518-7519).
proof_roadmap: Decompose an element of I cap J^2 (proof lines 7506-7512).
Apply the intersection lemma to the quadratic part (proof lines 7512-7518).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the intersection of an ideal with the square of a larger ideal under the hypothesis that the quotient of the two ideals is generated by an H1-regular sequence, and the proof is an 18-line argument in two steps. It chooses generators of the larger ideal modulo the smaller one, writes an element of the intersection in a three-part decomposition accordingly, observes that the middle part lies in the smaller ideal intersected with the ideal generated by the sequence, and then applies the intersection lemma of the same section to move that part into the product of the two ideals. The decomposition of the element and the application of the earlier intersection statement are the two ingredients, and both are displayed.
